originalTitle: Bill Miller's investing strategy: How the legendary fund manager outperformed the market for 15 straight years
simplifiedContent: A well-known investor, Bill Miller, was able to do better than the overall stock market for 15 years in a row. He achieved this by using a strategy that combines looking for undervalued companies, being patient, and going against the crowd. Miller focuses on finding companies with strong financials, such as good cash flow, and holding onto them until they reach a fair price or his reason for investing changes. This approach allowed him to outperform the market, which is a significant achievement. By understanding and replicating this strategy, individual investors may be able to make more informed investment decisions.

originalTitle: Utkarsh Small Finance Bank posts Rs 34 crore Q1 loss; asset quality stress persists
simplifiedContent: Utkarsh Small Finance Bank had a loss of Rs 34 crore in the first quarter of the year, which means it spent more money than it made. This is the fifth quarter in a row that the bank has lost money, which is concerning. The bank's loss is partly due to having many bad loans, which are loans that people or businesses are not paying back. The percentage of bad loans is still high at 6.1%, which is a problem for the bank. The good news is that the loss is smaller than it was before, but the bank still has work to do to fix its problems with bad loans.

originalTitle: Muthoot Finance reports 25% rise in Q1 profit, announces leadership transition
simplifiedContent: Muthoot Finance, a company that lends money to people using their gold as security, made 25% more profit in the first quarter of the year compared to the same time last year. They made a total of Rs 2,550 crore in profit, which is a significant increase. This growth is mainly due to more people taking out loans using their gold. The company is also changing its leadership, with Alexander George Muthoot set to become the new managing director on October 1, but this change still needs to be approved by the company's shareholders. This news matters because it shows that Muthoot Finance is doing well financially, which could be good for investors who own shares in the company.

originalTitle: Week Ahead: Wall Street eyes US jobs data, SpaceX debut earnings and Disney results
simplifiedContent: This week, investors are waiting to see how many new jobs were created in the US in July. This information is important because it will help investors understand what might happen to interest rates in the coming months. Interest rates are like the cost of borrowing money, and they can affect the stock market. Investors will be paying close attention to this news because it can influence their decisions about where to put their money. The jobs report is considered one of the most important economic releases of the week, and it will be closely watched by investors on Wall Street.

originalTitle: Sebi order against Zee likely to delay planned  ₹3,143-crore fundraise
simplifiedContent: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) has made a decision that will affect a company called Zee. Sebi has stopped Zee from buying or selling stocks and other investments for a certain period of time. This decision is likely to delay Zee's plan to raise ₹3,143 crore (a large amount of money) from investors. This matters because Zee was counting on raising this money, and now they will have to wait. The delay may impact Zee's plans and operations.

originalTitle: Yen Traders Brace for More Intervention With US at Japan’s Side
simplifiedContent: Some important countries, including Japan and the US, recently worked together to affect the value of Japan's currency, the yen. This effort, called an intervention, helped the yen's value go up quickly. Now, people who trade currencies are watching closely to see if Japan and the US will take similar action again when markets open in Asia. This matters because it can impact the value of the yen and potentially other investments. The traders are prepared for another possible intervention, which could further change the yen's value.
